title: Recovery paths that trusted stale flags, a documented check that never ran, and failures whose evidence was destroyed
what_went_wrong: --retry-failed re-billed on a stored restored=True flag without re-checking the current state (introduced in P8).
The stage hash file was per run+stage, so a later batch overwrote an earlier batch's hash.
A resume continued to later dates after a FAILED batch.
Resume killed OS processes but not server sessions; a killed client's statement keeps running on the server.
verify_frozen's P6-2g docstring claimed a source-content comparison that the code never made.
stage_restore deleted the current rows before discovering that its stage tables were missing.

The wrapper always dropped the fixture, so a failed suite's state was destroyed; the suite's cleanup helper dropped recovery tables after an unverified restore; A14 only tested an early exit branch; the builder check could not fail; the log said 'pre-reset state restored' even when it was not.
root_cause: Recovery decisions were based on recorded flags and process state instead of the data's current content and the server's sessions; documented checks were not compared with the code; failure handling favoured a clean box over keeping the evidence.
detection: Astra v8 (gpt-6-astra run 4897654); every claim re-verified against the source by the orchestrator on 2026-10-18 (P9 task doc §0, E1-E11).

correction.code: Per-batch hash files; retry and abandon compare current content with the batch's pre-reset hash; FAILED batches hold their stage tables; stage_restore refuses before DELETE when stage tables are missing; resume stops at FAILED; server-side fencing (KILL target sessions, kill stray mysql clients; never on live DBs); verify_frozen compares source_content_hash; wrapper keeps a failed fixture (--teardown-kept); suite cleanup drops only after a verified restore; A11 counts ERROR; builder check exits 1 on a difference; conditional log wording.
correction.verification: Suite 34/34 on a fresh fixture (A22, A22b, A23, A24, A25 new); terminal-path check PASS; unit test 20/20; builder check exit 0 clean / exit 1 planted.

rule: A recovery step must decide from the data's current content and the server's live sessions, never from a stored flag or a dead process; a documented check must be found in the code before it is cited; a failed run's state is evidence and is kept.
